summary: 429s observed when SSE multiplex falls back to short-polling during ephemeral key rotation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AuroraSearch reports recurring 429 throttles for a subset of traffic routed through our SSE multiplexing path. The service opens an SSE stream for low-latency inference but falls back to short-polling when ephemeral API keys rotate. During the fallback window a large fraction of requests receive 429s despite overall tenant quota remaining.

Impact:
- Intermittent user-facing latency and failures for real-time search assistants in two regions (us-west-2 primary, eu-west-1 failover).
- Spike in errors corresponds to ephemeral key rotation events (~every 90s for their ingestion pipeline).
- Customer reports session-level drops and negative downstream UX (timeouts in client).

Environment:
- AuroraSearch dedicated pool, prod-us-west-2 origin, edge-proxies in us-west and eu-west.
- Client uses SSE multiplex with automatic short-poll fallback when server signals reconnect during key rotation.
- Observed during morning ingestion window; customer runs ~120 concurrent short-lived agents.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Create 100 short-lived ephemeral API keys that rotate every 60-120s.
2) Start SSE multiplex connections from 120 agents in us-west.
3) Force key rotation (via signed URL refresh) while a portion of connections are mid-request; device clients detect SSE disconnect and immediately open short-poll HTTP/1.1 POSTs to the same route.
4) Observe intermittent 429s across ~10-25% of those short-poll requests for 30-90s after rotation.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include throttle headers showing per-route window exhaustion (X-Tokens-Remaining: 0) even though tenant-level quota shows headroom.
- Logs show duplicate accounting events from edge-proxy connection handoff and health-check probe increments for some connections.
- Throttling is concentrated on the short-poll fallback path; continuous SSE sessions that remain established do not see increased 429s.

Expected behavior:
- During ephemeral key rotation and transient fallbacks, requests should be accounted against the same token bucket semantics without double-counting due to connection-mode change.  Short-poll fallbacks should inherit per-connection grace or leverage burst credits rather than immediately hitting per-route windows.

Temporary workaround given to customer:
- Stagger ephemeral key refresh across agents (recommended: jittered refresh with backoff 5-20s).
- Increase short-poll window threshold on the dedicated pool via console route-weighting to provide burst headroom while we investigate.

Investigation notes (internal):
- Initial hypothesis: edge-proxy is creating a new accounting entry when SSE disconnect -> short-poll reconnect happens, and health-check/keepalive probes are also incrementing the same route counter, leading to double-counting inside the per-route token window.
- Correlated logs from edge-proxy and rate-limiter show session id mapping changes at time of rotation. A review of recent edge-proxy change (see PR in linked_github_prs) shows a small refactor in connection handoff logic that may affect token attribution.
- Reproduced in staging with synthetic jittered rotations; when health-checks were disabled on the test proxy the double-counts decreased.
- No evidence of tenant-level quota exhaustion; the issue is isolated to per-route windows and connection-mode transitions.

Proposed next steps:
1) Add temporary server-side suppressor: during detected key-rotation handoff window (configurable ~30s) merge new connection accounting to previous session id to avoid double-debit on per-route windows. (SRE + Edge team)
2) Patch edge-proxy to dedupe health-check increments and avoid incrementing route counters for probe endpoints. (Edge team)
3) Provide customer with detailed backoff pattern and a recommended ephemeral-key jittering doc. (Support/Docs)
4) Monitor dedicated pool for reduced 429 incidence after change; roll to prod in canary. (SRE)

Resolution notes (so far):
- Change 1 implemented as a canary on staging edge-proxies (edge-proxy v3.14.2-canary). Early staging tests show 80% reduction in double-counted increments under our synthetic load.
- Customer applied recommended jitter and reported partial improvement. Follow-up scheduled to roll patch to canary-prod for AuroraSearch dedicated pool after SRE sign-off.
